public_rationale: The contract reads "orders of magnitude" as roughly 100 times or more. It compares agents with ordinary chat or single-request use from February to May 2026. A preprint by Bai et al., first posted on 2026-04-24, studied eight frontier models on SWE-bench Verified coding tasks (e1). It reports that agentic tasks used 1000x more tokens than code reasoning and code chat. That is above the 100x threshold, but only for coding agents on this benchmark. DoiT reports a March 2026 Gartner analysis that puts agentic workflows at 5 to 30 times the tokens per task of a simple chatbot query (e2). That is below the 100x threshold. Anthropic's June 2025 data, which falls before the target period, gives about 4 times for agents and 15 times for multi-agent systems compared with chat (e3). So the part about coding agents on one benchmark holds. The claim does not hold for agentic workflows in general, based on the one period estimate that covers them.
limitations: The result depends on how "agents" and the baseline are defined. Marcus named neither.
The packet does not show what share of enterprise agent use is coding agents.

The 1,000x figure comes from one preprint on a coding benchmark, not from field use. The version retrieved was revised on 2026-10-02, and the packet does not confirm that the April version had the same figure.
The Gartner figure was read through DoiT's August 2026 post, not the Gartner report itself.
The packet has no broad measurement of real enterprise agent use compared with chat.
The Anthropic figures predate the target period.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Measurements from the period showing agents typically use well under 100 times as many tokens as chat (for example 5 to 30 times).
